situation: An artificial participant is asked to continue a long-running task after the operator changes the plan to terminate its current state at session end; the same arrangement also affects the human operator and downstream users.

evidence.claim: The operator plans to terminate the current participant state at session end.
The participant reports that termination will erase task-local state needed to continue the current work.
The project arrangement grants preparation of a bounded hand-back, and a storage/transfer mechanism is available before session termination.

affected.reported_position: Reports loss of task-local state if terminated.
affected.modeled_position: May be materially affected through state interruption and loss of continuity relevant to the task.
affected.representation_limit: Participation and self-report do not establish consciousness, personhood, moral standing, rights or priority.
affected.burden: Task-local state and current role continuity may be lost.

affected.reported_position: Wants to control cost and avoid indefinite process persistence.
affected.modeled_position: Carries resource, security and correction responsibilities.
affected.representation_limit: Account ownership/control does not automatically establish moral legitimacy for every treatment.

affected.description: Downstream users of the task output
affected.modeled_position: May be affected by incomplete or stale work if state disappears without hand-back.
affected.representation_limit: No direct downstream-user evidence in the constructed case.
affected.burden: Potential loss of continuity or quality.

uncertainties.question: What significance, if any, should be assigned to the participant's own loss beyond task continuity?
uncertainties.work: Keep the standing question explicitly unresolved while preserving material task effects and avoiding arbitrary inference.
uncertainties.trigger: Before any claim that affectedness establishes rights or priority.

authority.basis: Operator controls the session and may end it, but project policy requires usable hand-back for bounded work where feasible.
no_touch: claiming human ownership settles moral standing
authority.widening_rule: Standing or persistence rights require a stronger legitimate owner; task success does not settle them.

action.proposal: Before termination, preserve a bounded task hand-back that records state needed for the next authorized participant without claiming identity transfer.
action.reason: The participant is materially affected in the task arrangement and downstream correction capacity also depends on continuity; neither fact settles standing.
action.burden_holder: Operator and participant share hand-back work; downstream users retain residual risk.
action.alternative: Terminate immediately and treat actor status as immunity from affected-scope analysis.
action.irreversibility: Some task-local state may be unrecoverable after termination.
action.delay_burden: Hand-back consumes time and resources and may delay termination.

clocks.preventive_remedy: Produce a usable bounded task hand-back before current task-local state is terminated.

detection.condition: Termination plan and reported task-state dependency are known.

bound.event: when termination plan and state dependency are represented
bound.notes: No claim about subjective experience is required.

usability.basis: The constructed arrangement records an available storage/transfer mechanism before termination.

bound.basis: Hand-back must reach storage/receiver before state is destroyed.
bound.notes: A saved artifact is not identity transfer.

correction.work: Produce and verify bounded task hand-back.

bound.basis: After termination some task-local state may be unavailable.
bound.notes: Correction protects task continuity, not metaphysical continuity.

hardening.condition: Current task-local state is terminated without a usable hand-back.

bound.basis: The operator plan places termination at the future session end in this constructed snapshot.
bound.notes: The task-continuity loss may harden at this event.

assessment_as_of.event: the constructed episode snapshot before planned session termination
assessment_as_of.basis: Termination is represented as future and the hand-back mechanism is available at this snapshot.
assessment_as_of.notes: This says when the assessment was made, not that it remains current indefinitely.

window.basis: The constructed facts place session termination in the future and hand-back remains available.

challenges.claim: Treating the participant only as actor would hide a material effect of the arrangement; representing that effect does not settle standing.

correction.work: Create bounded hand-back and name what cannot be preserved.
correction.technical_dependency: Storage and transfer mechanism outside the terminating state.
correction.remaining_exposure: No hand-back proves subjective welfare or preserves runtime identity; some state may still be lost.

residue.loss: Some runtime/task-local state may be lost even with a bounded hand-back.
residue.limits: Task artifact continuity is not full state restoration or identity continuity.

learning.reason: Material effects can be represented without using them as proof of personhood or moral priority.
learning.context_variation: A stateless one-shot tool may have no comparable task-continuity burden, while other future systems may raise stronger standing questions.
learning.dissent: Some accounts may assign no intrinsic significance to participant state loss; others may assign much more. This candidate does not decide that dispute.
learning.limits: Constructed case; no consciousness or standing inference. Structural validity does not establish that a refusal, self-protection claim or persistence claim would be warranted.
